Improved lower bounds for the other models. Several other types of flips have been introduced in the literature (see e.g. [14] for an overview of the results in the different models). We proved that we can strengthen the best lower bounds in terms of the symmetric difference for two other types of flips: non-crossing flips and rotations. Let T be a spanning tree, e be an edge of T and f be an edge such that (T ∪ f ) \ e is non-crossing. We say that the flip is non-crossing if T ∪ f does not contain any crossings. In other words, we restrict to flips where the new edge does not cross the edge that is deleted. We say that the flip is a rotation if e and f share an endpoint. In other words, every flip must rotate an edge around a point in that case.
